title: THE VEIL AND THE GLORY THAT REMAINS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Moses finished speaking to them, he put a veil over his face. But whenever he entered the Lord's presence to speak with him, he removed the veil until he came out. And when he came out and told the Israelites what he had been commanded, they saw that his face was radiant. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the Lord." - Exod 34:33-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A rhythm forms. Moses goes in unveiled, comes out shining, speaks God's words, then covers his face again.

Paul explains what the veil was really about. Moses covered his face so the Israelites would not see the radiance fading away (2 Cor 3:13). The glory of that old covenant was real, but it was temporary. It faded.

And that is precisely why the new covenant is better. Its glory does not fade. Under Christ, Paul says, the veil is removed — and we all, with unveiled faces, contemplate the Lord's glory and are being transformed into His image with ever-increasing glory (2 Cor 3:18). Not diminishing. Increasing.

What Moses had for moments, we have permanently through the Spirit. What he had to hide, we are invited to reflect openly.

So the chapter that began with shattered tablets ends with a shining face and a covenant renewed. That is the direction God's story always moves — from brokenness to restoration, from fading glory to lasting glory, from the mountain to the Man who is the radiance of God's glory (Heb 1:3).

Live unveiled. There is nothing to hide behind anymore.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What veils do you still hide behind before God or others?
2. Do you live as though the glory is fading or increasing?
3. How can you deliberately behold Christ's glory this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that the veil is gone and Your glory does not fade. Transform me as I look to You. Amen.
